title: Flat algebraic-space derived pushforward and base change
statement: Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived direct image is computed by K-injective resolutions, and derived tensor pullback by K-flat resolutions. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Let $S$ be a scheme, $f:X\to Y$ a flat quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$, and $g:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ any morphism of algebraic spaces. Put $X^{\prime}=X\times_Y Y^{\prime}$, with projections $g^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to X$ and $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$. For every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, the canonical adjunction-mate map $\beta_E:Lg^*Rf_*E\to Rf^{\prime}_*L(g^{\prime})^*E$ is an isomorphism. These functors preserve quasi-coherent cohomology and the comparisons commute with identity and successive base changes under the canonical derived composition isomorphisms. For a proper flat finitely presented $f$, every $f^{\prime}$ is again proper flat finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 08IR, lemma-compare-base-change, flat (hence Tor-independent) case; sites-cohomology.tex Remarks 0E46, remark-compose-base-change, and 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, for composition. Stability of the morphism hypotheses: spaces-morphisms.tex lemmas base-change-proper, base-change-flat and base-change-finite-presentation.

proof.text: All derived pullbacks preserve quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. Let $u:Z\to W$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$. For an affine etale scheme $a:V\to W$ put $Z_V=Z\times_WV$, $b:Z_V\to Z$, $u_V:Z_V\to V$. The cited chart calculus gives $a^*Ru_*K\cong R(u_V)_*b^*K$, and $b^*K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Since $V$ is affine, $Z_V$ is quasi-compact by the definition of a quasi-compact morphism, and quasi-separated: its diagonal is the relative diagonal over $V$ followed by a base change of the closed immersion $V\to V\times V$, both quasi-compact. Thus [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-pushforward-right-adjoint], for the morphism $u_V$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated spaces, gives $R(u_V)_*b^*K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_V)$. Quasi-coherence of cohomology is checked on such a covering by the chart calculus, so $Ru_*K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W)$. This applies to $f$ and $f^{\prime}$: base change preserves quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, because affine-test inverse images and relative diagonals commute with fibre products.

source.place: 08FA (lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image) (1), local on the target; 08F4; duality-for-spaces.tex 0E55 for qcqs spaces; spaces-morphisms.tex 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), 03KR (quasi-separated over quasi-separated base).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-complex-base-change] to $f$, $g$, $E$ and the one-term complex $G^\bullet=\mathcal O_X[0]$. It is quasi-coherent and bounded above. It is flat over $Y$: for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ with image $\bar y$, flatness of $f$ on etale scheme charts makes $f$ flat at the image of $\bar x$, so $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}\to\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ is flat by [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness]. Its displayed isomorphism is $\beta_{E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_X}$ followed by $Rf^{\prime}_*$ of the tensor-pullback isomorphism and of $1\otimes(L(g^{\prime})^*\mathcal O_X\to(g^{\prime})^*\mathcal O_X)$. The complex $\mathcal O_X[0]$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], since tensoring with it is the identity; so it is its own K-flat resolution and the last map is the identity onto $(g^{\prime})^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X^{\prime}}$. Hence $\beta_{E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_X}$ is invertible. Naturality of the mate $\beta$ along the unit isomorphism $r:E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_X\to E$ gives $\beta_E\circ Lg^*Rf_*(r)=Rf^{\prime}_*L(g^{\prime})^*(r)\circ\beta_{E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_X}$, so $\beta_E$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: 0A1K (lemma-base-change-tensor) with G = O_X; 08IR (lemma-compare-base-change), flat case; spaces-morphisms.tex 04NG (lemma-flat-at-point-etale-local-rings).

proof.text: The coherent derived comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] identify the outer pullback square with the pasted inner squares. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clauses 1 and 2, to their pullback comparisons: taking mates gives exactly the composite of their exchange maps. For successive $g$ and $a$, this says $\beta_{ga,E}=\beta_{a,Lg^{\prime *}E}\circ La^*(\beta_{g,E})$ under the canonical composition isomorphisms. Clause 4 makes the identity comparison the identity. These are identities of the specified maps, not just existence of isomorphisms.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex 0E46 (remark-compose-base-change) and 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal); generic mate identities fill the omitted verification.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] says separately that flatness, properness and finite presentation survive every algebraic-space base change. Apply all three to the same $f$ and $g$ to obtain the last assertion.
